n:Golomt Bank: Golomt Bank is a commercial bank in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. It is linked to the Bank of Mongolia, the country's central bank, through a person who worked at both. Khosjargal Undraa spent thirteen years at Golomt Bank, then worked at MIG LLC and BPM Mongolia LLC, and later became a member of the Bank of Mongolia's Supervisory Board. That is a career move between a commercial bank and the central bank, not a finding against either.
n:Government of Chad: The Government of Chad sits in N'Djamena. It is linked to BEAC, the Bank of Central African States, which issues money for a group of countries in the region, through one person's career. Abbas Mahamat Tolli was Chad's Minister of Finance and Budget, and also president of the Development Bank of Central African States, before becoming Governor of the Bank of Central African States from 2017 to 2024. The record is a career move and carries no accusation.
n:Government of Côte d'Ivoire: The Government of Côte d'Ivoire sits in Abidjan. It shares one career with the BCEAO, the Central Bank of West African States, which issues money for several countries in the region. Tiemoko Meyliet Kone joined the BCEAO in 1975, was its National Director from 1991 to 1998 and its Governor from 2011 to 2022. Before returning he was Ivorian Minister of Construction, Urban Planning and Housing, and chief of staff to Prime Minister Guillaume Soro; after the BCEAO he became Vice-President of Côte d'Ivoire.
n:Government of Djibouti: The Government of Djibouti, in the capital Djibouti, fills the board of the Central Bank of Djibouti. Under the statutes set by law number 118/AN/11/6eme L of 22 January 2011, that board consists of the Governor plus six administrators appointed by decree, so every seat other than the Governor's is chosen by the executive. The bank's own 2024 annual report describes the board as its supreme organ and repeats that composition, citing the 2011 law. The arrangement has no end date.
n:Government of Malawi: The Government of Malawi sits in Lilongwe. It is linked to the Reserve Bank of Malawi, the country's central bank, by one person's career. MacDonald Mafuta Mwale was Secretary to the Treasury in the Malawian government before moving to the Reserve Bank, where he served as Deputy Governor and was then appointed Governor with immediate effect, as reported on 7 January 2025. That is a move between government service and the central bank, not an allegation of anything.
n:Government of Rwanda: The Government of Rwanda, in Kigali, is linked to two central banks through careers. John Rwangombwa was Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, and earlier Secretary to the Treasury and first Accountant General, before serving as Governor of the National Bank of Rwanda from 2013 until February 2025. Dr Ibrahim L. Stevens did macroeconomic advisory work for Rwanda's finance ministry before becoming Deputy Governor of the Bank of Sierra Leone in July 2014; he had been its Director of Research from 2008 to 2010, and later its Governor.
n:Government of Saint Vincent and the Gr: The Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines sits in Kingstown. It is linked to the ECCB, the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, which issues money for a group of island states, by one person's career. Sir Cecil Jacobs was the government's Financial Secretary before becoming Governor of the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, a post he held from 1973 to 1989. The connection is a move from a government finance post into the central bank.
n:Government of Tanzania: The Government of Tanzania sits in Dodoma. It shares a career with the Bank of Tanzania, the country's central bank. Emmanuel Tutuba was Permanent Secretary to the Treasury in the Ministry of Finance, and earlier budget commissioner in the same ministry, before being appointed Governor of the Bank of Tanzania on 7 January, in an appointment reported on 9 January 2023. That is a move from the finance ministry into the central bank, with nothing alleged against him.
n:Government of the Macao Special Admini: The Government of the Macao Special Administrative Region appoints the board of the Monetary Authority of Macao, which issues and manages the territory's money. Macao's Chief Executive, Sam Hou Fai, named Vong Sin Man, a worker of the Statistics and Census Service, to the Authority's board from 1 July to 31 December 2025. The order was made under article 50 of the Basic Law and the Authority's statute, approved by Decree-Law 14/96/M of 11 March 1996, under which the head of the executive appoints the board.
n:Government of the Union of the Comoros: The Government of the Union of the Comoros, in Moroni, shares control of the Central Bank of the Comoros with France. Under statutes signed in Paris on 22 April 2008 and still in force, the board has at most eight members, half designated by the French Government and half by the Comorian government. The Governor is named by the President of the Union, on the Finance Minister's proposal. New draft statutes approved on 28 June 2024 still awaited promulgation at year's end.
n:Halyk Bank: Halyk Bank is a commercial bank in Almaty, Kazakhstan. Its tie to the National Bank of Kazakhstan, the country's central bank, runs through Grigory Marchenko, who chaired the National Bank from October 1999 until 2004 and then became chairman at Halyk Bank. An article dated 30 January 2009 reported that he had been appointed to chair the central bank a second time. The movement between the two posts is a career record, not an accusation.
n:Investrust Bank Plc: Investrust Bank Plc is a commercial bank in Lusaka, Zambia. It is linked to the Bank of Zambia, the country's central bank, through one person's career. Dr Richard K. E. Chembe held senior management positions at the Bank of Zambia and at the International Monetary Fund, the lender that governments turn to for emergency loans, before becoming Managing Director of Investrust Bank Plc with effect from 1 May 2015. Nothing is alleged against him.
n:Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC: Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC is a bank in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Its tie to Bangladesh Bank, the country's central bank, is through Md. Khurshid Alam, who was appointed a Deputy Governor of Bangladesh Bank in February 2024 on a three-year contract and was forced to resign in August 2024. On 24 May 2026 he was appointed chairman of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC. The move between the two institutions is a career record, with no wrongdoing stated.
n:JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia: JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia is a commercial bank in Tbilisi, Georgia. It is linked to the National Bank of Georgia, the country's central bank, through Nino Jeladze. She worked at JSC ProCredit Bank Georgia and at ProCredit Holding in Frankfurt before joining the National Bank of Georgia, where she became head of the Supervisory Policy Department in 2024 and Vice-Governor and a member of the Board on 10 February 2025. That is a career move, not a complaint.
n:Joint Public Accounts Committee, Natio: The Joint Public Accounts Committee of Belize's National Assembly sits in Belmopan. Reporting on the Auditor General's report for April 2016 to March 2017, it prioritised significant material differences between Central Bank of Belize and SmartStream balances, of 42 million, 19 million, 3 million and 1.4 million dollars. At its March 2026 hearings Auditor General Maria Rodriguez said not even the Central Bank accounts were being reconciled. The 19,489,652.02 dollar difference for the Debt Service Escrow Account, the Committee recorded, was a typographical error, as the Auditor General confirmed.
n:Latin Securities: Latin Securities is a firm in Uruguay. Its tie to the Central Bank of Uruguay runs through Washington Ribeiro, who held three posts there: director from June 2010 to March 2020, vice president from March 2020 to July 2024, and president from July 2024 to March 2025. He then joined Latin Securities as head of Uruguayan macro and sovereign strategy. That is a move from the central bank into private finance, with nothing alleged.
n:Lithuanian parliamentary commission on: This was a commission of Lithuania's parliament, in Vilnius, set up to examine the collapse of the bank Snoras. Chaired by Valentinas Mazuronis, it found that the Bank of Lithuania, the country's central bank, acted too fast and with too little reasoning when it shut Snoras down in November 2011. Mazuronis said both the takeover of Snoras shares in the public interest and the start of bankruptcy proceedings were hasty and not sufficiently reasoned.
n:Mahmoud Abbas: Mahmoud Abbas is the President of Palestine, based in Ramallah, and he appoints the board of the Palestine Monetary Authority, which carries out central banking for Palestine. He issued a presidential decree reconstituting that board, acting on recommendations from the Cabinet and from the Authority's Governor. Three of the eight seats are held by virtue of law: the Governor, who chairs the board, the Deputy Governor, and a representative of the Ministry of Finance, named as Majdi Al-Hassan.
n:Maria Rodriguez: Maria Rodriguez is the Auditor General of Belize, based in Belmopan, the official who checks the government's accounts. At hearings of the National Assembly's Joint Public Accounts Committee in March 2026 she said that not even the Central Bank of Belize accounts were being reconciled, and pointed to differences between confirmation letters from the bank and the government's own records. She also confirmed that a 19,489,652.02 dollar difference recorded for the Debt Service Escrow Account was a typographical error, with no actual difference.
n:Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas de Gua: Guatemala's Ministerio de Finanzas Públicas, the finance ministry, is in Guatemala City. Alvaro Gonzalez Ricci was its Minister of Public Finance, a post he took up in January 2020, before becoming president of the Banco de Guatemala, the country's central bank. Emisoras Unidas reported on 1 October 2022 that he had taken the central bank post for a four-year term running to 20 September 2026. The move from ministry to central bank carries no allegation.
n:Ministry of Finance of Eswatini: The Ministry of Finance of Eswatini is in Mbabane. It shares a career with the Central Bank of Eswatini, the country's central bank. Martin Dlamini was Governor of the Central Bank from July 1997 to November 2013, and then became the country's Minister of Finance. That is a move from the central bank into the government department that manages public money, and nothing is alleged against him in connection with it.
n:Ministry of Finance of Moldova: The Ministry of Finance of Moldova is in Chisinau. It is linked to the National Bank of Moldova, the country's central bank, through Octavian Armasu. He was Moldova's Minister of Finance before being appointed Governor of the National Bank on 30 November 2018, for a seven-year term. The connection is a straightforward move from the finance ministry into the central bank, with no accusation attached to it.
n:Ministry of Finance of Montenegro: The Ministry of Finance of Montenegro is in Podgorica. It shares a career with the Central Bank of Montenegro. Radoje Zugic was the central bank's Deputy Director General for Payment System Operations from 2001 to 2004 and its Governor from 2010 to 2012, then served as Montenegro's Minister of Finance and afterwards as adviser to the Prime Minister. He returned as Governor of the central bank in October 2016. These are job changes, not findings against him.
n:Ministry of Finance of North Macedonia: The Ministry of Finance of North Macedonia is in Skopje. It is linked to the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia, the country's central bank, through Anita Angelovska Bezhoska. She managed the ministry's Treasury Department and was State Secretary there, and worked as an economist in the European Department of the International Monetary Fund, before becoming Vice-Governor and then Governor of the National Bank. That is a career path between ministry and central bank.
n:Ministry of Finance of Uzbekistan: The Ministry of Finance of Uzbekistan is in Tashkent. Timur Ishmetov has moved between it and the Central Bank of Uzbekistan more than once: he went from First Deputy Chairman of the Central Bank to First Deputy Minister of Finance, having earlier been First Deputy Chairman of the State Committee for Investments, and later served as Minister of Finance. He was then made Chairman of the Central Bank, with the appointment taking effect on 11 December 2024.
